description: City already tracks parking ticket offenders, making pay station use redundant.

description: Centralizes city fuel infrastructure management to Fleet Services.

chips.text: Councillor Danauer questioned capital and operating budget funding details.
Taxpayers will fund $2.5 million capital and $250,000 annual operating costs.

Administration will highlight fuel infrastructure budget items for Council.

description: Saskatoon's bridges and structures are mostly in good condition.
A $1.48 million funding shortfall exists for 2025.
A consolidated report will inform November budget decisions.

chips.text: Mayor Block highlighted proactive investment prevents costly future repairs.
Safety implications flagged for University Bridge if repairs are deferred.
A consolidated asset management report will be presented to GPC in September.

description: Saskatoon roadways are 63% good; 15% are very poor.
$74 million annually needed for roads, $8.5 million for sidewalks.
Sidewalk repairs now prioritize areas of greatest need.

chips.text: Staff noted combining sidewalk and road work did not save money, causing coordination delays.
Residents are affected by delays when road and sidewalk work is combined.
Staff corrected council's understanding that the indicative budget fully closed the funding gap.
City changed strategy to decouple sidewalk and road rehabilitation projects.
The optimal rehabilitation cycle for sidewalks remains an unanswered question.
Staff promised to clarify the optimal rehabilitation cycle for sidewalks.

description: City fleet faces a $10 million funding gap by 2030.

chips.text: Staff explained purchasing vehicles is often cheaper than leasing for seasonal use.
Administration will present options to close the fleet funding gap.
